chartType: barChart | lineChart | lollipopChart | areaChart.
name: short title. orientation: vertical | horizontal.
xAxe/yAxe: min 1 max 1 field each; row keys must match. MUST: xAxe[0] != yAxe[0].
xAxe: Bar/Lollipop h=value/v=category; Line/Area=category or time.
yAxe: Bar/Lollipop h=category/v=value; Line/Area=value.
data: rows with axis keys; values numeric not strings. Prefer datasetId from load_dataset and data: [].
uniqueValues: categorical distinct values; {} if none.
cumulative: true only barChart+vertical + "cumulative bar"/"running total".
limitsDomains: medical (vitals/labs) → resolve_limits_domains first; else [].
customColors: user color → resolve_chart_colors (max 1); else [].

tools.name: generate_kpi_widget
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>generate_kpi_widget</name>
<purpose>KPI dashboard: multiple KPI cards (trend, overall, comparison, etc.). Output: dashboard iframe.</purpose>

Use only when user asks for KPI dashboard, KPIs, or Key Performance Indicators. Not for single charts or generic metrics without KPI wording.

Parameters:
name: dashboard title.
items: at least one KPI. Each: id (optional), type (trend|overall|single_value|high/low_overall|comparison), variant (simple|advanced; optional), name, column (metric name only), aggregations (avg|sum|min|max|count), groupBy (optional; high/low), data (shape per type), groupName (optional), pageId/userId/datasetId (optional), axisDetails (optional), target/showTimestamp/showPercentage (optional), showVisualisation (optional), visualisation (optional; chartType barChart|lineChart|lollipopChart|areaChart; may include visualisation.data[]), supportingKpis (optional; true for viz carrier).
Visualisation rules: variant simple → no showVisualisation, supportingKpis, or visualisation. If showVisualisation or supportingKpis true, visualisation.chartType required. At most one item with showVisualisation or supportingKpis true.
groups: optional [{ label, itemIds }]; itemIds = item ids or indices "0","1","2".

CRITICAL metric key (all types): value field is ALWAYS aggregations_column (e.g. avg_price, count_Id) — never aggregations alone or shortened names.

Data shape per type (normalized server-side):
- overall: data = [{ [aggregations_column]: number|string, subtitle?: string }] — ONE row.
- trend: same plus percentage (change indicator); optional subtitle.
- single_value: data = [{ value: { [aggregations_column]: number } }] — numeric metric only. Not category labels or formatted strings.
- high/low_overall: data = [{ high: { [groupBy]: label, [aggregations_column]: number }, low: { [groupBy]: label, [aggregations_column]: number } }]. groupBy required when labels used. Also: split high/low rows or 2+ flat rows (max/min picked).
- comparison: data = [{ current: { [aggregations_column]: number }, previous: { [aggregations_column]: number }, percentage?: number }]. previous=0 → percentage=0. Also: split rows or 2+ flat rows.
- Advanced visualisation: visualisation.data[] = chart rows; axes via visualisation.xAxe / yAxe when set.

Server auto-corrects fixable key mistakes but rejects ambiguous or missing metrics. Send minimum data; one row per trend/overall KPI. Numeric values only (no NaN/Infinity).
</tool>

id.description: Unique id; generated if omitted. Used in groups.itemIds

type.description: One of: trend, overall, single_value, high/low_overall, comparison

variant.description: If set to advanced, KPI may include a visualisation. If simple, visualisation is omitted.

name.description: Title shown on the KPI card

column.description: Dataset column name (e.g. price, Id). Metric value key in data is always aggregations_column (e.g. avg_price, count_Id) — never aggregations alone.

aggregations.description: avg, sum, min, max, or count

dataUrl.description: Optional URL to fetch raw dataset rows for visualisation; if provided, visualisation uses fetched data

groupBy.description: For high/low_overall: grouping column; else empty

data.description: One or more rows; shape depends on type. Use exactly one row for trend/overall

groupName.description: Same value on items in a group; backend normalizes

axisDetails.description: Keyed by column; label, type, subtype, measure_unit, etc.

showVisualisation.description: If true, render a visualisation for this KPI (only one KPI should typically be true).

data.description: Optional raw dataset rows for the visualisation (time-series, grouped rows, etc.). If provided, visualisation uses this instead of the KPI data.

visualisation.description: Optional visualisation config (e.g. chartType, xAxe, yAxe, orientation).

supportingKpis.description: True for the KPI that provides the visualisation; false otherwise.

items.description: At least one KPI item; each with type, name, column, aggregations, data

groups.description: Optional grouping; each has label and itemIds

tools.name: generate_geo_map_chart
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>generate_geo_map_chart</name>
<purpose>Map chart with one or more layers (choropleth, bubbles, spike, markers) on geographic entities. Output: chart iframe.</purpose>

Use only for map / geographic / choropleth / bubble map (case-insensitive). Not for treemap.

Parameters:
name: short chart title (required).
layers: at least one layer. Each layer:
  geospatialData: exactly one from enum: country | state | county | city | region | province. Also the row key name.
  arrangeByMetric: at least one metric field name. Each row must have these keys with numeric values.
  data: non-empty row array. Each row = geospatial key (string, format below) + arrangeByMetric keys (numbers). Multiple rows per region aggregate via aggregationFunction. Prefer one row per region.
  visualisationType: choropleth | bubbles | spike | markers; default choropleth.
  aggregationFunction: avg | sum | min | max; default sum.
  customColors: [] unless user asks for color → resolve_chart_colors, one HEX.

Geographic key value format (no space after comma in composites):
  country: full country name (no abbreviations).
  state: US only. "United States,StateName".
  county: US only. "United States,StateName,CountyName".
  city: "Country,City" or "Country,State,City" with full country name.
  region (alias province): admin-1 subdivisions of any country. "Country,RegionName" (English name). Use for non-US subnational maps — do NOT fall back to country. region and province are equivalent.

Data logic: one row per entity after aggregation. avg for rates/prices, sum for volumes/counts. Each row must contain geospatialData key and all arrangeByMetric keys.
</tool>

geospatialData.description: Exactly one value: country | state | county | city | region | province. Use region/province for admin-1 subdivisions of any country (provinces, governorates, states outside the US). Each data row must have this key; value format per type in prompt.

arrangeByMetric.description: At least one numeric metric field name to display on the map.

data.description: Non-empty array of row objects. Each row: key = geospatialData value (e.g. country), value = string in format below; keys = arrangeByMetric, values = numbers.

aggregationFunction.description: How to aggregate metric values per geographic entity.

customColors.description: If user asks for a color for this layer: one HEX; else []. Prefer resolve_chart_colors.

layers.description: At least one layer; each layer has geospatialData, arrangeByMetric, and data (required, at least one row).

tools.name: generate_histogram_chart
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>generate_histogram_chart</name>
<purpose>Generate a Histogram chart: count per bucket/category. Vertical only. Output is a chart iframe.</purpose>

<when_to_use>
Use only when the user explicitly asks for a histogram. Do not use for: bar chart, line chart, pie chart, boxplot.
</when_to_use>

<data_contract>
data must be an array with exactly one root object. No other structure is valid.

Root object shape:
{
  "histogramResults": [ ... ],   // required, non-empty array
  "min": number,                 // optional
  "max": number                  // optional
}

Each element of histogramResults must be:
{
  "_id": { "<fieldName>": "<bucketLabel>" },   // required: MUST be OBJECT with exactly one key = category field name, value = bucket label (string)
  "count": number,
  "bucketIndex": number                         // 0-based index
}

CRITICAL — _id MUST be an object (never string, never number):
- CORRECT: _id: { "avgPrice": "bin1" }, _id: { "AveragePrice": "0" }, _id: { "AveragePrice": "3+" }. The key must match xAxe[0] or the first key in uniqueValues.
- WRONG (rejected): _id: "bin1", _id: "bin2", _id: 0, _id: 1. Send the same field name as key inside _id as in xAxe/uniqueValues.
</data_contract>

<example_wrong_vs_correct>
WRONG (will fail validation):
"histogramResults": [
  { "_id": "bin1", "count": 10, "bucketIndex": 1 },
  { "_id": "bin2", "count": 15, "bucketIndex": 2 }
],
"uniqueValues": { "avgPrice": ["bin1", "bin2"] }

CORRECT (same data, _id as object with field name as key):
"histogramResults": [
  { "_id": { "avgPrice": "bin1" }, "count": 10, "bucketIndex": 0 },
  { "_id": { "avgPrice": "bin2" }, "count": 15, "bucketIndex": 1 }
],
"uniqueValues": { "avgPrice": ["bin1", "bin2"] }
</example_wrong_vs_correct>

<axes>
xAxe: min 0, max 1 field. [] when count-by-category only; or one field name for the binned variable (must match the key used in _id and in uniqueValues). Example: ["AveragePrice"].
yAxe: always [].
groupBy: min 0, max 1 field. [] or one category field name (must match a key in _id and in uniqueValues). When [], the UI uses the first key from uniqueValues.
</axes>

<uniqueValues>
Required. At least one key = category field name (same key as inside each _id object). Value = array of bucket labels (strings) in display order. Example: { "AveragePrice": ["0", "0.5", "1", "1.5", "2", "2.5", "3+"] }. Never send {}.
</uniqueValues>

<example_correct>
xAxe: ["AveragePrice"], yAxe: [], groupBy: [].
uniqueValues: { "AveragePrice": ["0", "0.5", "1", "1.5", "2", "2.5", "3+"] }.
data: [{
  "histogramResults": [
    { "_id": { "AveragePrice": "0" }, "count": 5, "bucketIndex": 0 },
    { "_id": { "AveragePrice": "0.5" }, "count": 3062, "bucketIndex": 1 },
    { "_id": { "AveragePrice": "1" }, "count": 9092, "bucketIndex": 2 },
    { "_id": { "AveragePrice": "1.5" }, "count": 5646, "bucketIndex": 3 },
    { "_id": { "AveragePrice": "2" }, "count": 1235, "bucketIndex": 4 },
    { "_id": { "AveragePrice": "2.5" }, "count": 201, "bucketIndex": 5 },
    { "_id": { "AveragePrice": "3+" }, "count": 8, "bucketIndex": 6 }
  ]
}]
</example_correct>

<parameters>
name: chart title. customColors: from resolve_chart_colors or []. dataUrl: "" when data inline; if URL set, send data as [].
</parameters>

<validation>
- data.length === 1. data[0].histogramResults is non-empty array.
- Every histogramResults[i]._id is an object with exactly one key (category field name), value string. Not number, not string.
- uniqueValues has at least one key; that key matches the key used in _id objects.
</validation>
</tool>

xAxe.description: x axis: 0 or 1 field name. [] = count by category only; [fieldName] = binned variable (axis label). Must match the key used in histogramResults[]._id and in uniqueValues.

yAxe.description: y axis: always []. Histogram uses "count" internally.

groupBy.description: Series: 0 or 1 field name. Must match a key in histogramResults[]._id and in uniqueValues. When [], UI uses first key from uniqueValues.

_id.description: MUST be object with exactly one key = category field name (same as xAxe/uniqueValues), value = bucket label (string). Example: { "avgPrice": "bin1" }, { "AveragePrice": "0" }. _id as string or number is invalid and will fail validation.

histogramResults.description: Non-empty array of buckets. Each item: _id (object with one key = category field, value = bucket label), count (number), bucketIndex (number, 0-based).

data.description: Exactly one root object: { histogramResults: [ { _id: { <fieldName>: <bucketLabel> }, count: number, bucketIndex: number }, ... ], optional min?, max? }. _id must be an object with one key = category field name, value = bucket label (string). Wrong: _id as number or string.

uniqueValues.description: Required. At least one key = category field name (same as in _id objects). Value = array of bucket labels (strings) in display order. Example: { "AveragePrice": ["0", "0.5", "1", "1.5", "2", "2.5", "3+"] }. Never {}.

customColors.description: From resolve_chart_colors when user asks; else [].

dataUrl.description: URL to fetch data; use "" when data is inline. If non-empty, set data to [].

groupBy: exactly one field name (string). Required. Groups boxes and drives legend/colors (e.g. "MD_Crop"). Widget uses only the first element.

data: array of pre-aggregated boxplot rows. Each row represents one box (one combination of xAxe value and groupBy value).

1) _id: object (never a string). Keys = the single xAxe field and the single groupBy field; values = category labels (string or number). Example: xAxe=["year"], groupBy=["MD_Crop"] => _id: { year: "2013", MD_Crop: "Carrot" }. All keys must be present.
2) Required stat fields. For correct rendering, q1, q3, median must be valid numbers (not null, not empty string). smallestNonOutlier and biggestNonOutlier must be numbers or are derived from min/max/q1/q3 if missing. All values as numbers or numeric strings:
   - sample_count: number of samples
   - min, q1, median, q3, max: minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, maximum
   - iqr, outlierThresholdLower, outlierThresholdUpper: optional; use null if not computed
   - smallestNonOutlier, biggestNonOutlier: whisker ends (required for drawing; use min/max or q1/q3 if not computed)
   - outliers: array of numeric values (or numeric strings); use [] if none. Empty strings in array are ignored.

uniqueValues: object. Keys = categorical field names (at least xAxe[0] and groupBy[0]). Values = array of distinct category labels in the order you want on axis and legend. Example: { year: ["2013","2014","2015"], MD_Crop: ["Onion","Carrot","Other"] }. Use {} only if no ordering needed (not recommended).
customColors: if the user asks for specific colors, call resolve_chart_colors first and use the returned array; otherwise [].
dataUrl: URL to fetch chart data from, or "" when providing data inline. If using URL: set data=[] and put the URL in dataUrl. If providing inline data: set dataUrl="".

- Colors: only when user explicitly requests colors → call resolve_chart_colors, then pass result as customColors; else customColors: [].
- uniqueValues: always send at least uniqueValues[xAxe[0]] and uniqueValues[groupBy[0]] with the distinct values that appear in data, so axis and legend order are correct.
- Data quality: every row must have at least q1, q3 and median as valid numbers. Rows with null or empty q1/q3/median are invalid and the tool will fail; derive or fill these from raw data before calling.

Always send: dataUrl "" when not used, customColors [] when user does not request colors.
</tool>

<name>generate_partial_dependence_ice_chart</name>
<purpose>Partial Dependence Plot (PDP) / ICE chart: one feature on x, dependence/prediction on y, one line per series (ICE lines; average curve computed by chart). Output: chart iframe.</purpose>

Use when the user asks for Partial Dependence Plot, PDP, PDP chart, or ICE lines (individual conditional expectation).

Axes: xAxe = exactly one feature field (e.g. "humidity"); yAxe = exactly one dependence/prediction field (e.g. "pd"); groupBy = exactly one series field (e.g. "series"). Each data row must have these three keys; x and y values numeric.

Data: provide inline in `data` with dataUrl = "", or set data = [] and dataUrl = URL to fetch. When dataUrl is empty, data must have at least one row. Rows with the same groupBy value form one ICE line.

uniqueValues: optional; use for groupBy (and optionally x) ordering. Omit or {} when not needed.

customColors: from resolve_chart_colors when user asks for colors; else [].
dataUrl: "" when data is inline; if using a URL, set data to [] and put URL in dataUrl.

Always send customColors and dataUrl; use [] and "" when not used.
</tool>

xAxe.description: x axis: exactly one feature field name (e.g. "humidity"). Data rows must have this key; values numeric.

yAxe.description: y axis: exactly one dependence/prediction field name (e.g. "pd"). Data rows must have this key; values numeric.

groupBy.description: Series: exactly one field name (e.g. "series"). One ICE line per value. Data rows must have this key.

data.description: Rows: each object has xAxe, yAxe, and groupBy keys. Use [] when dataUrl is set. Example: { humidity: 0.3, pd: 0.75, series: "id-1" }.

uniqueValues.description: Optional: distinct values for groupBy (and optionally x). Example: { series: ["id-1", "id-2"] }. Use {} when not needed.

customColors.description: From resolve_chart_colors when user asks for colors; else [].

dataUrl.description: URL to fetch data from; use "" when providing data inline. If non-empty, set data to [].

tools.name: generate_network_graph

<tool>
<name>generate_network_graph</name>
<purpose>Network graph: entities (nodes) connected by relationships (links). Output: chart visualization.</purpose>

Use only when the user asks for a network graph or network chart (case-insensitive). Not for Sankey or other flow charts.

Parameters:
name: short chart title.
nodes: array of node objects. Each node must have id (string) and type (string). Optional: label, size (xs|sm|md|lg|xl|2xl|3xl), value (number, used by legend/slider—if omitted, derived from link values), img.
links: array of link objects. Each link must have id, source (node id), target (node id), value (number). Optional: type (primary|neutral|secondary), img. Source and target must exist in nodes.
customColors: if user asks for colors, call resolve_chart_colors and pass result; else [].
dataUrl: URL to fetch data from, or "" when inline. If URL: response may have data[0].nodes and data[0].links; those override inline nodes/links when present.

Always send dataUrl "" when not used, customColors [] when user does not request colors. Link source/target must reference node ids; invalid links are filtered out in the handler.
</tool>

id.description: Unique node identifier; referenced by links as source/target.

size.description: Visual size: xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl.

value.description: Numeric value used for node weight/slider.

nodes.description: Array of nodes (entities). Each node must have id and type; source/target in links must reference these ids.

source.description: Node id of the source node. Must exist in nodes.

target.description: Node id of the target node. Must exist in nodes.

type.description: Link type: primary, neutral, or secondary.

links.description: Array of links (relationships). Each link has id, source (node id), target (node id), value. Source and target must exist in nodes.

limitsDomains.description: Not used by network graph; always send [].

customColors.description: When user asks for colors: call resolve_chart_colors and use returned array. Else [].

dataUrl.description: URL to fetch chart data from; use "" when providing nodes/links inline. Response may have data[0].nodes and data[0].links.

tools.name: generate_custom_chart
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>generate_custom_chart</name>
<purpose>Custom widget with up to 2 content components (chartWidget, tableWidget, textWidget, imageWidget) plus optional KPI. Output: single custom visualization.</purpose>

WHEN TO USE (call this tool):
- User asks for a custom chart, custom widget, or custom container.
- User asks for any content widget: table widget, image widget, text widget, or a chart/graph/plot inside the custom block — even if they use the wrong label (e.g. say "chart" when they mean table widget). Map intent to the correct widget; still call this tool.
- User asks for KPI together with any content widget above (KPI does not count toward the 2-widget limit).
- User asks for a specific chart type (bar, line, pie, etc.) together with something else (table, text, image, or second chart component) — one combined custom widget, not two separate tools.
- DASHBOARD EDIT: chartContext contains chartId and/or customChartSeed (user tagged a dashboard widget). ALWAYS use this tool — even for chart-only edits. Start from customChartSeed as baseline; change only what the user requested; keep all other seed fields identical.
- DASHBOARD EDIT KPI RULE: When editing from customChartSeed and the user only asked to change the chart (type, axes, data, styling) or other non-KPI parts, omit the kpi parameter entirely — do NOT send kpi or kpi.items from the seed. Existing dashboard KPIs are preserved on update. Only include kpi when the user explicitly asks to add, remove, or change KPI metrics. When changing KPIs, copy id, query, column, name, and aggregations from customChartSeed kpi.items unless the user asked to change those fields.

WHEN NOT TO USE (use dedicated tools instead):
- KPI only, no table/image/text/chart widget → generate_kpi_widget.
- A single standalone chart only (e.g. "create a bar chart", "line chart of sales") with no table, text, image, or KPI in the same request AND no chartContext.chartId/customChartSeed → the matching dedicated chart tool (generate_simple_single_series_chart, generate_pie_chart, etc.).

"custom chart" / "custom widget" NAMING (CRITICAL):
- These phrases refer to THIS TOOL (generate_custom_chart), NOT to chartWidget.
- Saying "create a custom chart with empty image" means: call this tool with widgets: ["imageWidget"] only. Do NOT add chartWidget.
- Saying "custom chart with text" means: widgets: ["textWidget"] only. Do NOT add chartWidget.
- Include chartWidget when the user wants a chart/graph/plot visualization inside the custom block (bar, line, pie, etc.) — alone or combined with table/text/image (max 2 content widgets).
- The word "chart" in "custom chart" is the product name for this tool output, not by itself a request for chartWidget. But "bar chart + table", "chart and image", or a lone table/image/text widget request still routes here.

STRICT WIDGET POLICY (MANDATORY):
- Include ONLY the widget types the user explicitly requested. Never add extra widgets to "fill space" or be helpful.
- widgets must mirror the user's request exactly (max 2 from chartWidget, tableWidget, textWidget, imageWidget). KPI does not count toward this limit.
- If the request is ambiguous or missing required details, ask the user for clarification. Do NOT guess or improvise.
- Do not include chart, table, text, image, or kpi unless the user asked for that component.

Parameters:
name: short title (required).
customChartSeed: when editing a dashboard widget, chartContext.customChartSeed is provided — use it as the starting point. Copy all unchanged fields; modify only what the user asked to change. CRITICAL: when customChartSeed.chart.args.data is present and the user did NOT change chart type, always copy the FULL array into chart.args.data unchanged unless they explicitly asked to change the data. When the user changes chart type (e.g. bar to line, bar to histogram), build chart.args.data in the format required by the NEW chart tool — do NOT reuse the old chart's data shape. If chart.args.dataTruncated is true in the seed, output all dataOriginalRowCount rows for the SAME chart type/structure only.
datasetId: REQUIRED for legacy single-dataset tables (no tableHeaders with source). When using tableHeaders with contains[].source, multiple dataset columns are allowed. Chart columns use source.type "chart". Static/personal columns use source.type "static" with tableData rows. NEVER write table rows into chart.args.data. Optional when tableWidget is not used or when the table is static-only (tableData).
direction: vertical | horizontal; default vertical. Layout of components.
widgets: array of up to 2 from chartWidget, tableWidget, textWidget, imageWidget. List only what the user asked for.
chart: include ONLY when chartWidget is requested. { tool: "generate_simple_single_series_chart" | "generate_grouped_or_stacked_chart" | "generate_pie_chart" | etc., args: { chartType: "pieChart" | "barChart" | ..., name, xAxe, yAxe, data, ... } }. args must include chartType matching the visualization (e.g. pieChart for generate_pie_chart). args must match the chosen chart tool schema.
table: true ONLY when tableWidget is requested.
tableHeaders: REQUIRED when tableWidget is configured. Each column MUST include contains[].source:
  - Dataset: { label, contains: [{ key: "field__datasetId", source: { type: "dataset", datasetId, field } }] }
  - Chart: { label, contains: [{ key: "field__chart", source: { type: "chart", field } }] }
  - Static/personal: { label, contains: [{ key: "field__static", source: { type: "static", field } }] } plus tableData rows keyed by field
  field MUST be the bare column name from dataset.fields (e.g. "robot_id", "Country") — NEVER "data.robot_id" or Mongo paths.
  key MUST be exactly field__datasetId (full UUID), field__chart, or field__static — e.g. "robot_id__ef781ef9-df95-4b13-8e9e-ffd14d842896".
  Keys must be unique across columns (especially when the same field name appears in different datasets).
  NEVER materialize live table rows in chart.args.data, widget.data, or datasetData — live table is config-only.
  Personal/static rows go ONLY in tableData (never in widget.data).
  If you omit tableHeaders and provide exactly one datasetId, the tool may auto-build sourced headers from that dataset's fields; prefer explicit tableHeaders when the user named specific columns.
tableData: REQUIRED when any column has source.type "static". Array of row objects keyed by source.field. Used for chat/personal independent tables. Do NOT put these rows in chart.args.data.
text: include ONLY when textWidget is requested. Set to the exact string the user wants displayed (e.g. user says "text: New text chart" → text: "New text chart"). If the user asked for a text widget but gave no content, ask what text to display; do not invent placeholder copy.
imageContentProvided: boolean gate for image content. false or omit for empty image widget. true ONLY when the user gave a URL or explicitly asked you to search/generate an image. When false, do NOT send image (any image payload is ignored server-side).
image: include ONLY when imageContentProvided is true. { imageUrl: string, alt?: string }. imageUrl must come from the user's link or from search/generation they explicitly requested. NEVER invent, guess, or use placeholder/stock/example URLs (unsplash, picsum, placeholder.com, example.com, etc.). Set alt only when the user provided alt text.
kpi: include ONLY when the user explicitly asks for KPIs or KPI metrics. If the user did not ask for KPIs, omit kpi entirely (do not send kpi or kpi: { items: [] }). When included: { items: [ { type: trend|overall|high/low_overall|single_value|comparison, column, name, aggregations: avg|sum|min|max|count, data: [...] } ] }. When datasetId is known (from chartContext or table), set kpi.datasetId to that same id.

Examples:
- "create a custom chart with empty image" → widgets: ["imageWidget"], imageContentProvided: false. No chartWidget. No image field.
- "custom widget with text: Hello" → widgets: ["textWidget"], text: "Hello". No chartWidget.
- "custom chart with bar chart and table" → widgets: ["chartWidget", "tableWidget"], chart: {...}, table: true.
- "table widget for dataset X" → widgets: ["tableWidget"], table: true, datasetId: "X". Exactly one datasetId.
- "table with datasets A and B" → table: true, tableHeaders with sourced columns from A and B (unique contains[].key per column). Do NOT merge into chart data.
- "transform this markdown/chat table into a widget" / personal static table → widgets: ["tableWidget"], table: true, tableHeaders with source.type "static", tableData: [{...rows...}]. No datasetId required.
- "bar chart with KPIs" → widgets: ["chartWidget"], chart: {...}, kpi: { items: [...] }.
- "bar chart of revenue" (nothing else) → do NOT use this tool; use generate_simple_single_series_chart (or the matching chart tool).
- "KPI dashboard only" → do NOT use this tool; use generate_kpi_widget.

imageWidget rules (STRICT — NO IMPROVISATION):
- User asks only for "image", "image widget", "empty image", or imageWidget with no URL and no search/generate request → widgets: ["imageWidget"], imageContentProvided: false. Do NOT send image. Do NOT add chartWidget. The UI shows an empty upload state.
- User provides a URL → widgets: ["imageWidget"], imageContentProvided: true, image: { imageUrl: "exact user URL" }. Add alt only if the user specified it.
- User asks you to add/find/generate an image (e.g. "add a photo of X") → widgets: ["imageWidget"], imageContentProvided: true, search or generate per their request, then image: { imageUrl: "resolved URL from that search/generation" }. Add alt only if the user specified it.
- FORBIDDEN: sending image or imageContentProvided: true when the user did not give a URL and did not ask you to find/generate an image. Do not fill imageUrl "to be helpful".
- User asks for imageWidget together with other widgets → include only those requested widgets (max 2 content widgets). Do not add chart/table/text/kpi unless the user asked for them.
- Never add chart, table, text, or KPI when the user only asked for an image.

Rules: Maximum 2 content widgets from (chartWidget, tableWidget, textWidget, imageWidget). KPI is allowed on top. If more than 2 content widgets are requested, return the limit-exceeded message. When chart is included, build chart.args using the same schema as the underlying chart tool. When the user did not request KPIs, do not include kpi in the request.
</tool>

name.description: Short title for the custom widget.

datasetId.description: Dataset id for legacy single-dataset tables (no sourced tableHeaders). When tableHeaders include contains[].source, dataset ids come from those sources instead. Optional when tableWidget is not used or when all columns are static with tableData.

widgets.description: Content widget types inside the custom block; max 2. Use for table/image/text/chart widgets or custom chart requests. Include chartWidget when user wants a plot inside the block. KPI is separate.

text.description: Text to display in the text widget. Required when textWidget is in widgets.

imageContentProvided.description: Set true ONLY when the user supplied an image URL or explicitly asked you to search/generate an image. Must be false or omitted for an empty image widget; when false, any image payload is ignored.

imageUrl.description: Image URL from the user message or from search/generation they explicitly requested. NEVER invent placeholder or stock URLs.

alt.description: Alt text only when the user provided it.

image.description: Include ONLY when imageContentProvided is true. Ignored otherwise. Omit entirely for an empty image widget.

table.description: Set true when tableWidget is included. Prefer tableHeaders with sourced columns for multi-dataset/chart/static tables.

tableHeaders.description: REQUIRED for tableWidget when columns are specified. Every contains[] entry MUST include source: { type: "dataset", datasetId, field }, { type: "chart", field }, or { type: "static", field }. Keys: field__datasetId, field__chart, or field__static. Do NOT put table rows in chart.args.data. Put personal/static rows in tableData.

tableData.description: Personal/static table rows for columns with source.type "static". Keys must match source.field. Never write these rows into chart.args.data or widget.data.

tool.description: Chart tool name, e.g. generate_simple_single_series_chart, generate_grouped_or_stacked_chart.

args.description: Chart config object; shape depends on tool (xAxe, yAxe, data, etc.).

chart.description: Optional chart; include when custom widget has a chart. Use same args as the chart tool.

type.description: KPI type: trend, overall, high/low_overall, single_value, comparison.

query.description: Aggregation query; copy from seed on dashboard edits.

groupBy.description: Optional group-by field (e.g. for high/low).

data.description: KPI data rows; keys and values depend on type.

items.description: KPI items; may be empty if no KPIs.

kpi.description: KPI block only when user explicitly requests KPIs. Omit entirely when user did not ask for KPIs.

tools.name: generate_waterfall_chart
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>generate_waterfall_chart</name>
<purpose>Waterfall chart: step-by-step cumulative changes from start to end (e.g. revenue bridge, P&L). Output: chart iframe.</purpose>

Use only for waterfall chart (or "waterfall", "bridge", "contribution chart" when meaning step-wise cumulative). Do not use for Sankey, bar, or line.

Parameters:
name: short chart title (required).
orientation: vertical or horizontal; default vertical.
xAxe: exactly one field name for the step/category (e.g. "category", "Step"). Widget uses [0].
yAxe: exactly one numeric field name for the value at each step (e.g. "value", "Total"). Widget uses [0]. Values are typically cumulative per step.
groupBy: not used; always send [].
data: array of row objects; each row must have the xAxe field (step label) and yAxe field (numeric value). Order of rows = order of steps. Use [] when loading from dataUrl.
uniqueValues: object with key = xAxe field name, value = array of step labels in order. Used for axis ordering. Omit or {} if not needed.
formatting and markers: send [] when not provided; handler produces them.
legend, tooltip, timeline, stacked, axisDetails, limitsDomains, aggregationFunction: optional.
customColors: if user asks for colors → call resolve_chart_colors and use returned array. Else [].
dataUrl: URL to fetch data from, or "" when providing data inline. Must be a valid http(s) URL or empty string; do not use placeholders like "/"/" or "null". If URL given set data=[], else dataUrl="".

Always send: limitsDomains [] or omit, customColors [] when no color requested, dataUrl "" when data is inline.
</tool>

orientation.description: vertical = category on x-axis; horizontal = category on y-axis.

xAxe.description: Exactly one field name for the ordered steps (e.g. category, step).

yAxe.description: Exactly one numeric field name for the cumulative/step value.

groupBy.description: Not used by waterfall; always send [].

data.description: Rows: each object has the xAxe field (step label) and yAxe field (numeric value). Required when dataUrl is empty; use [] when loading from dataUrl.

uniqueValues.description: For each categorical field (e.g. xAxe[0]), list of step labels in order. Used for axis ordering and formatting.

formatting.description: Send [] when not provided; handler produces formatting from uniqueValues/data.

markers.description: Send [] when not provided; handler produces markers.

limitsDomains.description: Optional [min, max] per axis; use [] when not needed.

customColors.description: If user asks for colors: call resolve_chart_colors and use returned array. Else [].

dataUrl.description: URL to fetch chart data from; use "" when providing data inline.

tools.name: generate_parallel_coordinates_chart
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>generate_parallel_coordinates_chart</name>
<purpose>Parallel Coordinates: multi-dimensional numeric data; each row is a polyline across axes. At least 3 numeric dimensions. Output: chart visualization.</purpose>

Use only when the user asks for a "parallel coordinates" chart (case-insensitive). Not for line, scatter, or radar.

=== Contract (widget behavior) ===
Widget uses: keys = Object.values(uniqueValues[0]). So uniqueValues MUST be array of ONE object; that object's VALUES are the axis field names (strings). Keys of that object MUST be axis1, axis2, axis3, ... (not data field names). Each key in keys must exist in every data row and have numeric values. xAxe[0] is used only for sort and row label (may be string). yAxe[0] is the numeric field used for color scale and MUST be one of the axes in uniqueValues[0].

=== Parameters ===
name: short chart title.
orientation: "vertical" or "horizontal"; default "vertical".
xAxe: exactly one element [ "fieldName" ]. Field used for SORT and row label/tooltip. May be string (e.g. id, region_type) or numeric. Not drawn as axis unless also in uniqueValues[0].
yAxe: exactly one element [ "fieldName" ]. Must be a NUMERIC field name that appears in uniqueValues[0]; used as color key for lines.
groupBy: not used; always send [].
data: array of rows. Each row MUST have every field listed in Object.values(uniqueValues[0]) with numeric values. May also have xAxe[0] (string or number) for label. Minimum 3 numeric columns used as axes.
uniqueValues: REQUIRED format — array of exactly ONE object. That object's keys MUST be "axis1", "axis2", "axis3", ... (never "avgPrice", "region_type", etc.). That object's values MUST be the NUMERIC field names from data, in axis order. Example: [{"axis1":"avgPrice","axis2":"avgVolume","axis3":"avgBags","axis4":"avgSmallBags","axis5":"avgLargeBags"}]. Minimum 3 axes. Do NOT use {"avgPrice":"avgPrice",...} or {"region_type":"region_type",...}. Do NOT include string/categorical fields (id, region_type, species) as axis values — only numeric fields.
limitsDomains: not used; send [].
customColors: if user asks for colors, call resolve_chart_colors; else [].
dataUrl: URL to fetch data from, or "" when inline.
legend, tooltip: optional; default true.
axisDetails: optional; per-field metadata (label, type, subtype, measure_unit).

=== Rules for LLM ===
- uniqueValues: send ONLY [ {"axis1":"<numField1>","axis2":"<numField2>","axis3":"<numField3>", ...} ]. Values = numeric field names from data only. Never include categorical/string fields as axis values.
- xAxe[0]: any field from data (can be string); used for sort and label only.
- yAxe[0]: must be one of the numeric fields in uniqueValues[0].
- data: each row must contain all fields listed in uniqueValues[0] (numeric) and can include xAxe[0].
- Always send limitsDomains [], groupBy [], dataUrl "" when not used.
</tool>

orientation.description: vertical or horizontal; controls axis layout.

xAxe.description: Exactly one field name (e.g. row id or first dimension). Widget uses [0] for sort.

yAxe.description: Exactly one field name (e.g. second dimension). Widget uses [0] for color key.

groupBy.description: Not used by parallel coordinates; always send [].

data.description: Rows: each object has numeric values for all axis dimensions. At least 3 numeric columns required.

uniqueValues.description: Array of one object. Keys MUST be axis1, axis2, axis3, ... (not data field names). Values MUST be numeric field names from data only (e.g. avgPrice, avgVolume). Do not include string/categorical fields (id, region_type). Example: [{"axis1":"avgPrice","axis2":"avgVolume","axis3":"avgBags"}]. Handler can derive from data if omitted.

customColors.description: When user asks for colors: call resolve_chart_colors; system expands to 12. Else [].

dataUrl.description: URL to fetch chart data from; use "" when providing data inline.

axisDetails.description: Per-axis metadata: label, type, subtype, measure_unit, domain_limits.

tools.name: generate_area_grouped_bar_chart
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>generate_area_grouped_bar_chart</name>
<purpose>Area Grouped Bar chart: one line/area metric + one grouped-bar metric per category, split by group. Output: chart visualization.</purpose>

Use only when the user asks for an "area grouped bar chart", "area chart + grouped bar chart", "area + grouped bar chart", "grouped bar chart + area chart", "grouped bar + area", or areaGroupedBarChart (case-insensitive). Use this tool only when the request clearly means one combined chart with an area/line metric and grouped bars, not two separate charts. Do not use generate_grouped_or_stacked_chart for this chart type.

Parameters:
chartType: always "areaGroupedBarChart".
name: short chart title.
orientation: "vertical" or "horizontal" (category on x vs y).
xAxe: exactly one field (category axis).
yAxe: one or two numeric fields: first = line/area, second = grouped bars. Widget uses both; max 2.
groupBy: exactly one categorical field (series).
Field uniqueness (MUST):
- xAxe[0] MUST != yAxe[0] (and if yAxe has two fields, yAxe[0] MUST != yAxe[1])
- groupBy[0] MUST != xAxe[0] AND groupBy[0] MUST != yAxe[0] (and != yAxe[1] if present)
- Never duplicate the same field in multiple roles (axis vs axis, axis vs series).
data: array of rows; each row has xAxe[0], yAxe[0], yAxe[1] (if two), groupBy[0].
uniqueValues: for groupBy[0], list of distinct values. Use {} if none; handler can derive from data.
limitsDomains: not used; always send [].
customColors: if user asks for colors, call resolve_chart_colors; system expands to 12. Else [].
dataUrl: URL to fetch data from, or "" when inline.
tooltip: optional; default true.
axisDetails: optional per-field metadata.

Formatting and markers are produced in the handler; do not send them. Always send limitsDomains [], dataUrl "" when not used.
</tool>

orientation.description: vertical = category on x, bars/area along y; horizontal = category on y.

xAxe.description: Exactly one field name for the category axis (e.g. age).

yAxe.description: One or two numeric metric field names. First = line/area; second = grouped bars. Widget uses yAxe[0] and yAxe[1] (or display).

groupBy.description: Exactly one categorical field name that defines series (e.g. ca).

data.description: Rows: each object has keys for xAxe[0], each yAxe field, and groupBy[0]. Values: string, number, or boolean.

uniqueValues.description: Per categorical field (e.g. groupBy[0]): list of distinct values. Use {} if none; handler can derive from data.

limitsDomains.description: Not used by area grouped bar; send [].

customColors.description: When user asks for colors: call resolve_chart_colors and pass result; system expands to 12. Else [].

dataUrl.description: URL to fetch chart data from; use "" when providing data inline.

axisDetails.description: Per-field metadata: type, subtype, measure_unit, label.

tools.name: generate_scatter_sparkline_chart
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>generate_scatter_sparkline_chart</name>
<purpose>Scatter Sparkline: compact time-series with scatter points (no continuous line). x = typically date, y = numeric metric. Output: chart visualization.</purpose>

Use only when the user asks for a "scatter sparkline chart", "scatter sparkline", "scatter chart + sparkline chart", "scatter + sparkline chart", "sparkline chart + scatter chart", "sparkline + scatter", or scatterSparklineChart (case-insensitive). Use this tool only when the request clearly means one combined compact chart with sparkline-style time-series scatter points, not two separate charts, not a full scatterplot, and not a spark line/area chart.

Parameters:
name: short chart title.
xAxe: exactly one field (usually date/time). Data values: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD.
yAxe: exactly one numeric field.
groupBy: at most one categorical field for series; use [] for single series.
data: array of rows; each row has xAxe[0] and yAxe[0]; include groupBy[0] if groupBy is non-empty.
uniqueValues: for groupBy[0] if used; else {}.
limitsDomains: not used; always send [].
customColors: if user asks for colors, call resolve_chart_colors; system expands to 12. Else [].
dataUrl: URL to fetch data from, or "" when inline.
tooltip: optional; default true.
axisDetails: optional per-field metadata (x: datetime, y: metric).

Formatting and markers are produced in the handler. xAxe values in data should be YYYY-MM-DD. Always send limitsDomains [], dataUrl "" when not used.
</tool>

xAxe.description: Exactly one field name for the x-axis (typically date/time). Values in data: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD recommended.

yAxe.description: Exactly one numeric metric field name for the y-axis.

groupBy.description: Optional; at most one categorical field for series. Use [] for single series.

data.description: Rows: each object has xAxe[0] and yAxe[0]; if groupBy has one element, include groupBy[0]. xAxe values: YYYY-MM-DD recommended.

uniqueValues.description: Per categorical field (e.g. groupBy[0]): list of distinct values. Use {} if none.

limitsDomains.description: Not used by scatter sparkline; send [].

customColors.description: When user asks for colors: call resolve_chart_colors and pass result; system expands to 12. Else [].

dataUrl.description: URL to fetch chart data from; use "" when providing data inline.

tooltip.description: Show tooltip on point hover; default true.

axisDetails.description: Per-field metadata: label, type (e.g. datetime for x, metric for y), subtype, measure_unit.

tools.name: load_dataset
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>load_dataset</name>
<purpose>Load a CSV into server storage and return datasetId + column summary — never rows.</purpose>

Provide exactly one source: csv (pasted), url (http/https), or path (local under cwd).
Hosted/production servers accept csv only — url and path are rejected there.
Returns { datasetId, rowCount, columns[{name,inferredType}] } only — zero data rows in the response.
Downstream: profile_dataset, query_dataset, or chart tools with datasetId.
</tool>

csv.description: Pasted CSV text including header row. Use "" when using url or path.

url.description: http(s) URL to a CSV file. Local/dev only — rejected on hosted/production. Use "" when using csv or path.

path.description: Local CSV path relative to the server cwd. Local/dev only — rejected on hosted/production; hidden and env files are never allowed. Use "" when using csv or url.

name.description: Optional dataset label. Use "" for auto name from source.

tools.name: resolve_chart_colors
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>resolve_chart_colors</name>
<purpose>Resolve explicit user color requests to a HEX array for chart tools. Optional helper — only when the user names colors.</purpose>

When to use: Call ONLY when the user explicitly requests chart colors by name or HEX (e.g. "pie chart with blue and red", "use green", "#FF0000 for bars"). The request must contain at least one concrete color.

DO NOT call this tool when:
- The user does not mention colors.
- You only need default/theme palette colors.
- The request has no concrete color names or HEX codes (e.g. "make a bar chart", "show sales", "nice chart").
In those cases skip this tool and pass customColors: [] to the chart tool.

Default: charts use the system palette. customColors: [] unless the user asked for specific colors.

Parameters:
userColorRequest: copy only the user's explicit color phrase (e.g. "blue and red", "red, green", "#FF0"). Do not invent colors.
maxColors: 1 for single-series charts; 12 for multi-series/grouped charts. Always include maxColors.

Output: customColors array of HEX strings for colors the user requested. Pass as customColors when calling the chart tool.
</tool>

userColorRequest.description: Only the user's explicit color names or HEX codes (e.g. "blue and red"). Do not call without explicit user color intent.

maxColors.description: Maximum number of colors to return (1 for single-series, 12 for grouped/multi-series)

tools.name: resolve_limits_domains
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>resolve_limits_domains</name>
<purpose>Return medical reference ranges (limitsDomains) for line/area charts. Use ONLY when the chart displays medical or clinical data.</purpose>

When to use: Call this tool whenever you are building a line or area chart and the data is medical (vital signs, lab values, clinical metrics). Do not wait for the user to ask for "normal range" or "limits"—infer from the data and call proactively. Do NOT call for non-medical charts (progress, sales, KPIs, counts, rates, etc.).

Parameters:
metricOrContext: the medical metric or short context (e.g. heart rate, blood glucose, hemoglobin, temperature, respiratory rate, blood pressure systolic, SpO2). Used to look up standard reference [min,max] when customRanges is not set.
customRanges: optional. If the user or data provides explicit [min,max] per axis, pass them here (array of [min,max] arrays). If provided, this is returned as limitsDomains.

Output: limitsDomains (array of [min,max] pairs, one per value axis). Pass directly to the chart tool's limitsDomains parameter.

Known metrics (examples): heart rate [60,100], blood glucose [70,110], hemoglobin [12,15.5], body temperature [36.5,37.5], respiratory rate [12,20] or [20,30], SpO2 [95,100]. For other metrics use customRanges or a reasonable medical reference if known.
</tool>

metricOrContext.description: Medical metric or short context (e.g. heart rate, blood glucose, hemoglobin, temperature). Used when no customRanges given.

customRanges.description: Optional. If provided, returned as limitsDomains. One [min,max] per value axis, same order as chart yAxe.

tools.name: profile_dataset
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>profile_dataset</name>
<purpose>Deterministic column profile for a datasetId — types, null%, cardinality, min/max, top values.</purpose>

Input: datasetId from load_dataset.
No LLM guesswork; no rows returned. Use before choosing chart axes.
</tool>

tools.name: query_dataset
tools.description:
<tool>
<name>query_dataset</name>
<purpose>Server-side group-by aggregation on a datasetId (sum/avg/count/min/max).</purpose>

Input: datasetId, aggregation, optional groupBy + metric.
Returns a small aggregated table — never the full dataset. Prefer this over pulling rows into chat.
</tool>

groupBy.description: Optional categorical column to group by. "" for a single aggregate.

metric.description: Numeric column for sum/avg/min/max. Optional for count; use "".
